No published Rydberg-series ionization-energy measurement by that group was located (web search + arXiv listing).

Cook et al. Phys. Rev. A 98, 053415 (2018): could not be located/opened; the 1S0-1P1 frequency result found is Cook et al. PRL 121, 053001 (2018) (abstract only; full text paywalled, so the measured hyperfine constants/linewidth of 1P1 from that paper are not recorded).

Isotope shift of the 234.9 nm line (9Be-10Be, 9Be-7Be): no measurement located; only theory (Puchalski et al. PRA 89, 012506, 11Be-9Be value quoted second-hand). The only measured neutral-Be isotope shifts found are 10Be-9Be shifts of two-photon 2s2 1S0 - 2sns 1S / 2snd 1D Rydberg transitions (Wen, Travis, Lucatorto, Johnson, Clark, PRA 37, 4207 (1988)); the abstract gives no per-line numbers.
Measured hyperfine constants of 2s2p 1P1 and 2s3s 3S1: none located (theory values from arXiv:2603.11098 entered and marked).

Measured g_J of the 2s2p 3P levels: not stated in the Blachman & Lurio abstract or in the papers that re-analyse it; full text of Phys. Rev. 153, 164 is paywalled. Only LS/MCDHF theory values (3P1,2: 1.5000; 1P1: 1.0000; 3S1: 2.0000; arXiv:2603.11098 Table V) were seen, not entered.

Lifetime of 2s2p 3P0: no value located (for 9Be it decays only by hyperfine-induced E1; searched for neutral-Be hyperfine-quenching rates, found only Be-like ions). 3P1 and 3P2 lifetimes are theory only.

Measured lifetimes of 2p2 1D2, 2s3s 1S0, 2s3p 1P1, 2s3p 3P: none listed in the experiment column of Table IV of arXiv:2603.11098 and none found by search; theory values entered. The original beam-foil papers (Andersen 1969 'mean lives of 11 states in Be I', Bromander 1971, Hontzeas 1972, Bergstrom 1969) are paywalled and their abstracts contain no numbers, so they may hold further values not captured here.
Martinson, Gaupp & Curtis, J. Phys. B 7, L463 (1974) 1P1 lifetime: page not openable (IOP blocked) and not quoted in the opened tables.
Irving et al. Can. J. Phys. 77, 137 (1999) original page returned HTTP 403; its 1P1 lifetime 1.77(5) ns and f = 1.40(4) are taken from two secondary tables.
Photoionization cross sections / saturation parameters for 235 nm loading: not searched in depth.
notes: All energies identifying levels are copied from data/nist/Be_I_levels.tsv. 9Be is the only stable isotope (I = 3/2). Hyperfine sign convention: A and B of 2s2p 3P1,2 are the Blachman-Lurio constants AFTER second/third-order corrections for hyperfine mixing among the 3P_J levels (A negative because the 9Be nuclear moment is negative). First-order constants fitted directly to the same intervals (A1 = -140.1564, B1 = -3.2363, A2 = -124.6165, B2 = 0.7800 MHz; Puchalski et al. 2021) are a different definition - do not mix. The abstract of arXiv:2411.13013 quotes the old B(3P2) as 1.427(9) MHz while its Table VI and arXiv:2603.11098 give 1.429(8) MHz; the table value is used. Fine structure of 2s2p 3P: Blachman & Lurio (abstract) deduced W(3P2)-W(3P1) = 71.86(24) GHz and W(3P1)-W(3P0) = 19.41(19) GHz from the magnetic-field dependence of the hyperfine structure (not a direct measurement); Puchalski et al. 2021 calculate 71.379 and 19.498 GHz and suspect the experimental 3P2-3P1 value is inaccurate; the NIST level differences are 2.335 and 0.615 cm^-1. Lifetimes taken from Table IV of arXiv:2603.11098 are marked 'compilation' with the original paper named; for multiplets the measurement is a term value and is repeated on each J level. Where several measurements exist the laser (cascade-free) result is the main value and beam-foil results are in 'alternatives'; for 2p2 3P, 2s3d 1D and 2s4d 1D the main value is Bromander 1971 (a re-analysis of the Bergstrom 1969 Stockholm decay curves). The 2s5d 1D2 and 2s6d 1D2 beam-foil lifetimes disagree strongly with theory. 1S0-1P1: all three laser measurements (Cook 2018, Cook 2020, Ahrendsen 2024) agree; they are centre-of-gravity values limited by unresolved hyperfine structure. The line has natural width about 88 MHz; NIST ASD lists Aki = 5.52e8 s^-1, consistent with the measured 1.85(4) ns lifetime. Photoionization loading of 9Be+: neutral Be needs 9.3 eV (133 nm); the standard scheme is resonance-enhanced two-photon ionization with two 235 nm photons, the first resonant with 2s2 1S0 - 2s2p 1P1 and the second ionizing non-resonantly from 1P1. CW source (28 mW at 235 nm, twice-doubled 940 nm diode laser): Lo, Alonso, Kienzler, Keitch, de Clercq, Negnevitsky, Home, Appl. Phys. B 114, 17 (2014), arXiv:1306.3780 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1306.3780). Pulsed source (60 ns, 150 nJ pulses near 235 nm, frequency-quadrupled Ti:sapphire; 266 nm non-resonant two-photon ionization also discussed): Wolf, Studer, Wendt, Schmidt-Kaler, Appl. Phys. B 124, 30 (2018), arXiv:1711.01060 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.01060). Isotope shifts: Wen et al. PRA 37, 4207 (1988) (abstract, https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.37.4207) measured 10Be-9Be shifts in the 1S and 1D Rydberg series by resonance-ionization mass spectrometry and inferred a finite-mass correction to the ionization energy of 10Be of 270(40) MHz. Forbidden decays (theory, Fuhr & Wiese 2010 Table 4): M2 line 2s2 1S0 - 2s2p 3P2 at 4549.33 A (vacuum) A = 1.66e-04 s^-1; M1 within 2s2p 3P: 3P1-3P2 1.74e-10 s^-1, 3P0-3P1 4.83e-12 s^-1.
